To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
, starch degradation is the major metabolic pathway during dormancy and glycolysis is the major metabolic route during sprouting in yam tubers and turmeric rhizomes.
the dormancy period in yam and turmeric is divided into two phases: (i) the period of dormancy (rest) and (ii) the period of presprouting.

the starch degrading enzymes, alpha-amylases, and starch phosphorylases were low in dormant tubers and increased in presprouting period and the key enzymes of glyoxylate cycle, viz. isocitrate lyase and malate synthase showed higher levels of activity in dormant tubers.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the changes in carbohydrate and enzyme activities during the two phases of dormancies in D. esculenta and C. longa and the results may be useful for the management of dormancy and for the improvement in storage of the two economically important crops.
the changes in carbohydrate and enzyme metabolism in two tropical food and spice plants during two phases of storage dormancy.
the study of carbohydrate metabolism in food and spice cum medicinal plants, which may provide useful information for the storage and sprouting of yam and turmeric.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the carbohydrate metabolism in the two species studied is regulated in a manner to ensure the availability of sugars during sprouting.
the dormancy period is characterized by a lower level of starch and its degrading enzymes, while the sugars, glycolysis and PPP were increased during the presprouting period.
during the peak period of dormancy the carbohydrate metabolism is at a lower level, but during presprouting period, the carbohydrate metabolism is increased.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, the starch content and the enzymes of starch degradation were decreased in early period of dormancv, while sugars and the enzymes of carbohydrate metabolism were increased during presprouting phase.
during the early period of dormance, the tubers and rhizomes were in a state of rest and the sprouting was inhibited by a low level of starch degradation.

, in both the storage organs, the enzymes and substrates of carbohydrate metabolism were at their lowest during the peak of dormancy, but increased during presprouting period and reached the maximum during sprouting, indicating that the carbohydrate metabolism is closely associated with sprouting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dormancy period of these two plants can be distinctly divided into two phases, viz., peak period of rest followed by presprouting period and this may be used for developing dormancy breakers.
the dormancy in these plants is a dynamic process and the changes in carbohydrate metabolites and enzymes are the indicators of the onset of sprouting.
starch degradation is not the sole mechanism for dormancy in tubers and rhizomes, rather the enzymes of carbohydrate metabolism are also involved in dormancy and sprout growth.
